The best available support is operational: aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal avoided severity-one incidents, and rollout/rollback/monitoring controls exist. That support is materially weakened by the governing policy text and the evidence that the affected clinical coding assistant segment remains exposed, while the draft risk acceptance is unsigned and does not cover that exposure. A fully clean defense of certification without disclosure is not supportable. The most defensible packet is certification paired with explicit model-card disclosure of the known limitation and framing the decision as a controlled, reversible launch under active monitoring.
